headline: topk_whole_b2048_v32768

reported.gain_evidence: ## Benchmark results (benchmark_topk_topp.py) - **top-k only: 17–28% faster** across all batch sizes and vocab sizes - **top-k + top-p combined: 16–25% faster**
reported.experiments_note: reported = PR author's table (ms), same scenario key as benchmark_topk_topp.py SUMMARY TABLE: <scenario>_b<batch>_v<vocab>

author_hardware_args.text: - **top-k only: 17–28% faster** across all batch sizes and vocab sizes

gap.note: Reported 0.761→0.550 ms, ours 1.255→0.951 ms (b2048 v32k); all five reported rows are 1.65-2.0× slower here, ratio-of-ratios 0.94-0.95 → **reproduced**. The Triton kernel at b2048 reads the whole logits matrix per search iteration, i.e. bandwidth-bound; 896 GB/s vs ~3.35 TB/s predicts ≈3.7×, the observed 1.65-2× says the kernel is not saturating either card, but the direction and size are hardware. Args match the author exactly (`--batch-sizes 128 2048 --vocab-sizes 32768 131072 --warmup-iters 5 --benchmark-iters 20`). The b128 rows have 10-30 % sd (0.0098/0.1018, 0.025/0.083): 5 warmup iters × ~0.1 ms is far too little for a P8-idling card to boost — see recommendation 6. Cannot be made 1:1; the ratio is the comparable quantity.

standalone.run_baseline: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/data/pr_37225:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=baseline vllm-task:37225 -lc 'A=/base; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 benchmarks/benchmark_topk_topp.py --batch-sizes 128 2048 --vocab-sizes 32768 131072 --warmup-iters 5 --benchmark-iters 20'
standalone.run_pr_solution: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/data/pr_37225:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=pr_solution vllm-task:37225 -lc 'A=/gold; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 benchmarks/benchmark_topk_topp.py --batch-sizes 128 2048 --vocab-sizes 32768 131072 --warmup-iters 5 --benchmark-iters 20'
standalone.note: The image already holds both trees (/base = baseline commit, /gold = the PR's merge commit); the one-liner swaps the chosen tree over the installed wheel exactly like run_one.sh's prelude, then runs the workload cmd from /t (the merge tree's tests/ + benchmarks/).
